Schumer’s remarks were in response to news that Trump had signed an executive order exempting Russia from the sanctions legislation Congress passed last month.

Bipartisan opposition to the Russia sanctions waiver
Opposition to the order crossed party lines.
Sen.
Thom Tillis
(R-N.C.) called the move "beyond irresponsible" on X. He noted the Senate passed the law 86-11.

Beyond irresponsible. What part of enforcing a law passed 86-11 by the Senate does the President and his advisors not understand? It’s unconscionable that this administration is capitulating to a Russian dictator who illegally invaded Ukraine and butchers innocent civilians every…
Sen.
Richard Blumenthal
(D-Conn.), who helped pass the bill, called it a "craven, cowardly action."

These waivers have nothing to do with our national security, & everything to do with sucking up to Vladimir Putin. I hope my Republican colleagues will join me in condemning this craven, cowardly action. 2

Lindsey Graham
(R-S.C.), for whom the act is named, "would be appalled."
Lindsey would be appalled: Trump Signs Order Exempting Russia From Sanctions Law

Thomas Massie
(R-Ky.) backed the order in a post on X. He called the sanctions law "short-sighted" and said he was among only seven Republicans who voted against it.
"Glad to see Trump has used the executive authority granted to him by Congress to waive almost all of the provisions of this stupid law that pertain to Russia," Massie wrote.

What the waiver means for energy markets
Tariffs on buyers of Russian energy could affect oil, diesel and commodity flows. The order follows a deal allowing Russia to sell diesel to the U.S. and global markets amid fuel shortages.
